principles: Progressive overload means repeatable improvements in reps, load, range, or control while technique and recovery remain sound. These are starting ranges, not rigid prescriptions.
volumeCaveat: Count hard sets only when finished near 0-4 reps in reserve (RIR). Beginners often grow on the lower half of ranges. Add volume only when performance/recovery supports it.

doubleProgression.protocol: Choose a rep range (e.g. 8-12). Keep load fixed while adding reps. Once every work set reaches the top with clean form for 2 sessions, add the smallest practical load and return toward the lower end.
doubleProgression.tempo: Controlled eccentric around 2-3 sec; no mandatory pause unless needed for control.

autoregulaton.beginner: Most work sets at RIR 2-3; avoid frequent failure on compounds.

plateau: If load, reps, and quality stay flat for 2-3 sessions, check setup, sleep, food, and exercise order. Reduce sets or load for a 1-week deload if fatigue is accumulating; then resume below prior fatigue, not with forced maxes.

backAnatomy.width: Lats (especially shoulder adduction/extension), teres major; use vertical pulls and shoulder-extension rows with elbows toward hips.
backAnatomy.thickness: Rhomboids, middle/lower trapezius, rear delts, spinal erectors; use supported rows with controlled scapular retraction and hip hinges as appropriate.

pullUpRoadmap: Build 3 x 8-12 sec active hangs and scapular pulls.
Use assisted pull-ups or band assistance for 3 x 5-8, 2-3 min rest.
Add controlled eccentrics 3 x 3-5 only if shoulders tolerate them.
Reduce assistance after reaching all reps with full range for 2 sessions.
Practice unassisted singles with 2-3 min rest; stop before form degrades.

fourPartCues.setup: Set contact points, stance, grip, and equipment before the rep.
fourPartCues.bracing: Brace around the trunk; keep ribs and pelvis controlled for the movement.
fourPartCues.execution: Move through a repeatable pain-free range with the intended joint action.
fourPartCues.commonMistakes: Avoid momentum, lost positions, shortened range, and loading beyond current control.
